fields.name: User
fields.evidence: bg3.exe+0x2D10A20 (esv::timeline::FadeSystem) creates one component on a new entity (bg3.exe+0x2D124E0, default = the invalid user id constant) per user of an esv::timeline::DeferredEndingStateComponent whose fade-in finished or timed out, and stores the 4-byte user id.

fields.name: Fade
fields.evidence: bg3.exe+0x2D10A20 copy-constructs it from the string at +0 of the deferred ending state (default empty, capacity 15).

fields.name: field_20
fields.evidence: bg3.exe+0x2D10A20 copies the dword at +0x50 of the deferred ending state. The consumer bg3.exe+0x3451800 (query of added PlayerFadeInEventOneFrameComponent, called from the per-frame update of esv::script::GameplayEventSystem) calls every registered listener with (component, component + 8, this dword).

open_questions: field_20: probably the dialog instance id (same values as esv::timeline::DeferredEndingStateComponent+0x50, live 1..0x11C), not proven; the listener of esv::script::GameplayEventSystem was not identified.
Registered as a regular component (ComponentTypeIdContext) although named OneFrame.
second_pass: Offsets and widths are Windows-side (bg3.exe+0x2D10A20 writer, bg3.exe+0x3451800 reader passing +0, +8 and the dword at +0x20); 24 live instances agree (user 0x10001 at +0, STDString at +8). STDString is a builtin of generate.py now (24 bytes), so the earlier external_types override was removed.
